title: The price of reversing a renovation decision

blocks.text: A regional library board picks branch renovations each year with a small MILP: each renovation has a cost and a benefit, the year's budget is fixed, and renovations required by accessibility law are mandatory. Branch managers keep asking the same two questions: "why was my renovation left out?" and "why did theirs get in?". The board wants one answer to both: what the best plan would lose if that one decision went the other way, and which renovations would change.

`renovations.py` already has the board's model (`build`) and `best`, which solves a model and returns the best value and the chosen names, or `None` when no plan is feasible. `best` solves at a relative gap of 0, so both values in a cost are proven optima, as the lesson requires. Write `forcing_cost(items, budget, name)`. It returns a dictionary:

items: `"action"`: `"out"` if the best plan chose `name`, `"in"` if it did not;
`"cost"`: the best plan's value less the best value with that decision reversed, rounded to an integer, or `None` when no plan allows the reversal;
`"dropped"` and `"added"`: the names in the best plan but not in the reversed one, and the other way round, each sorted; both empty when there is no reversed plan.

blocks.text: The board's model, with $`R`$ the renovations, $`M \subseteq R`$ the mandatory ones, $`c_r`$ and $`v_r`$ each renovation's cost and value, and $`B`$ the budget:
Write the one row your reversal adds, with its label, for each of the two actions. Then code it: add it as a named row to a fresh copy of the model. The tests use their own branches.

cases.says: a renovation left out is forced in: the cost against the best plan, and what is dropped and added
a renovation the best plan chose is forced out, not in
forcing out a mandatory renovation has no feasible plan, so it has no cost
forcing in a renovation that cannot fit the budget has no feasible plan either

origin.section: A Forced Re-Solve Says What Gives Way, and the Rules Say Why

concepts: the cost of a decision is the best value lost when the opposite decision is forced and the model re-solved
a forcing is a named row added to a fresh copy of the model, never an edit of the solved plan
